items.last: I went through the whole ingestion pipeline. The reader parses the CSV in chunks of 10k rows. Each chunk goes through validation, which is where most of the time goes. Validation compiles its regexes on every call, which is wasteful. I also noticed the writer flushes after every single row. That flush is synchronous, so it blocks the async runtime. Together these account for roughly 80% of the runtime in the profile. The rest is spread evenly and not worth chasing. Do you want me to fix the regex compilation and the flushing?

Here's what I found in the image pipeline. Thumbnails are generated synchronously in the request handler. Each one decodes the full-size image, even for tiny previews. The resize uses a high-quality Lanczos filter, which is slow but looks good. Results are never cached, so the same thumbnail is rebuilt on every page view. The S3 upload happens in the same request too. I measured about 900ms per upload on average. Moving thumbnails to a background job would fix most of it, and caching would fix the rest. Should I do both, or only one of them?

Here's the full picture of why the build broke. The CI image was updated last night. It now ships OpenSSL 3 instead of 1.1. Our `openssl-sys` version only knows how to find 1.1 headers.
